Preprint — arXiv:2611.05665v1 [cs.SE]; short (4-page) preliminary study, no venue stated
Heidelberg University (Berndt, also affiliated with SAP; Baltes); Dalhousie University (Ralph); SAP (Bach)

Evaluates; secondary: Conceptual — document-based qualitative analysis of the construct validity of nine agentic coding benchmarks (constructs claimed, metrics operationalizing them, additional task attributes as potential confounders), with recommendations and future plans; no agent run

fields.v: No SDD approach and no agent configuration. Objects analysed: nine benchmarks taken from the model cards of Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 4 Argon (Table I): DeepSWE v1.1, FrontierCode v1.1 extended, FrontierSWE v2, SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA, SWE-bench Multilingual, SWE-bench Multimodal, SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 4.0, Vibe Code Bench

N/A (no approach). Benchmark task inputs described: natural-language task specifications or issue descriptions (e.g. FrontierCode, SWE-Atlas, Vibe Code Bench web application specifications), with tests, rubrics or browser workflows as verifiers
N/A (no approach). Study method: dataset of benchmarks from model cards; qualitative extraction of constructs and metrics (RQ1); extraction of additional task attributes (RQ2)
N/A
Not run, document-based (benchmark introductory publications and public datasets analysed)
Not classifiable (no specification-driven approach; authors do not use SDD terms)

N/A (no tasks run). Benchmarks analysed cover existing repositories (issue resolution, long-horizon implementation, Q&A, test writing, refactoring), terminal tasks and new web applications from specifications
Nine benchmarks (eight for RQ1, FrontierSWE excluded; seven for RQ2, FrontierCode also excluded); benchmark sizes from 34 tasks (FrontierSWE) to 1865 tasks (SWE-bench Pro)
General software engineering benchmarks (multiple open-source and proprietary repositories, several programming languages, CLI tasks, web applications)
N/A (no participants; one author annotated with LLM assistance)
None

None measured. Benchmark metrics catalogued (Table II): pass rate (7 of 8 benchmarks), FrontierCode weighted rubric score, SWE-Atlas rubric-set pass rate, Vibe Code Bench workflow accuracy (workflow passes when at least 90% of substeps succeed)
None measured. Rubric items covering test quality, scope discipline, codebase conventions, maintainability and code quality noted in FrontierCode and SWE-Atlas
None

Construct (target label) claimed or inferred per benchmark (Table II); number of benchmarks reporting each additional task attribute: repository (6 of 7), task category, programming language (4 of 7), task difficulty (2 of 7), task specificity (Fig. 1)

Manual qualitative analysis of the introductory benchmark publications, combining human annotation with LLM-based analysis (LLM not named): one author read the papers and extracted or inferred the constructs; supporting quotes in the supplementary material; task attributes extracted from the public datasets
N/A (document-based; no configuration run)

N/A (no configurations compared). Benchmarks compared on constructs, metrics and reported task attributes, framed by the ACM SIGSOFT Empirical Standards components for benchmarks (quality, metrics, measurement procedure, task sample)

N/A for configurations. Findings: explicit constructs only for DeepSWE and SWE-bench Multilingual, inferred for the others; broad constructs (coding / SE capability) operationalized with one or two aggregate metrics, mostly pass rate; reported task attributes vary between benchmarks (lack of standardization); scores should be read as evidence for the specific capabilities exercised, not general SE capability

N/A for configurations. Method caveats stated: inferred labels reflect the authors' interpretation, not constructs defined or validated by the benchmark authors; validation procedures and measurement models not systematically audited (their omission does not imply absence); FrontierSWE (insufficient information) and FrontierCode (dataset not public) excluded

Limitations: preliminary study; constructs inferred by one author; validation procedures not audited. Gaps: benchmarks rarely define target constructs; missing evidence on content validity, factor structure, predictive relationships and score stability; lack of standardized task attributes undermines comparability; need code-quality metrics (static analysis vs LLM judges) and benchmarks of long-term effects of agent use (e.g. ISO/IEC 25010); planned empirical assessment of the factor structure of coding-ability constructs and of task description quality

No reporting inconsistencies found; Table II lists eight benchmarks after excluding FrontierSWE, consistent with text. Supplementary material (quotes used to label each benchmark) on Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23599441 (p. 2, ref. [30]). No pre-registration. No programming language (no code written)
